title: Contra Palladium Arianum Libri Duo
author: Vigilius of Thapsus
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0293d.stoa006.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Diu citra acta tractavimos. Et quoniam tanta sacrilegia a Patre Palladii et Secundiani nostris auribus ingeruntur, ut difficile quisquam credat tam aperte eos blaspbemare potuisse : vel ne qua ipsi calliditate dicta sua postea negare conentur, licet de tantorum sacerdotum testificatione dubitari non queat: tamen quoniam omnibus episcopis placet, fiant acta, ut unusquisque professionem suam postea negare non possit.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: For a long time we have been discussing without records being kept. And since such great sacrileges are being poured into our ears by Palladius and Secundianus against the Father that anyone would find it hard to believe that they could have blasphemed so openly, or lest they should by some cunning later try to deny what they have said, although the testimony of such great bishops cannot be doubted, nevertheless, since it pleases all the bishops, let records be made, so that no one may afterwards deny his own profession.
passages.notes: "a Patre" is awkward; perhaps corrupt (e.g. for "adversus Patrem" or a misplaced phrase). Translated as "against the Father". "tractavimos" read as "tractavimus", "blaspbemare" as "blasphemare".

passages.original: 486 Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Disceptationes nosiræ ei re firmandae sunt scripto imperiali, ut allegentur.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Our debates are to be confirmed in writing for the emperor, so that they may be submitted.
passages.notes: "486" is a page or column number from the printed edition and is omitted. "nosiræ ei re firmandae" read as "nostrae et firmandae" or similar; the text seems garbled, and the sense is uncertain.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Ecce quod Cbristianus constituit imperalor. Noluri injuriam facere sacerdotibus : ipsos interpretes constituit episcopos. Ac per hoc, quoniam in sacerdotali concilio consedimus, responde ad ea quae tibi proponuntur. Arii epistola lecta est: etiam nunc recitabitur, si tibi videtur. A principio habet blasphemias, solum Patrem æternum dixit. Si tibi videtur quod Dei Filius sempiternus non sit , hoc ipsum quemadmodum vis astrue : si damnandum putas, damna Evangelium.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: See what a Christian emperor has decreed. He did not wish to do injury to the priests: he appointed the bishops themselves as the interpreters. And therefore, since we have sat together in a priestly council, answer the things that are put to you. The letter of Arius has been read; it will be recited again even now, if you wish. From the beginning it contains blasphemies: it said that the Father alone is eternal. If it seems to you that the Son of God is not everlasting, establish this very point in whatever way you wish; if you think it should be condemned, condemn [it] by the Gospel.
passages.notes: "damna Evangelium" literally reads "condemn the Gospel". This is probably a scanning error for "damna Evangelio" ("condemn [it] by the Gospel"), or the phrase may be ironic; the translation is uncertain.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Qui sunt consortes vestri ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Who are your associates?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Interim quia superioribus temporibus concilium sic factum cst, ut Orientales in Orientis partibus constituti haberent concilium, Occidentales in Occidente , nos in Occideatis- partibus constituti convenimus ad Aquileiensium civitatem juxta imperatoris præceptum. Denique etiam praefectus Italiæ litteras dedit, ut si vellent convenire, in potestate haberent.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Meanwhile, since in former times the council was held in such a way that the Easterners, being established in the regions of the East, held a council, and the Westerners in the West, we, being established in the regions of the West, have assembled at the city of the Aquileians in accordance with the emperor's order. Moreover, the prefect of Italy also issued letters, so that if they wished to assemble, it would be in their power [to do so].

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Utique jussit, qui non prohibuit huc venire.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: He certainly ordered [it], who did not forbid [them] to come here.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Non opus est evagari diutius; responde nanc. Bene dixit Arius solum æternum Patrem? et secundum Scripturas hoc dixit, an non?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: There is no need to wander off any longer; answer now. Did Arius speak rightly in saying that the Father alone is eternal? And did he say this according to the Scriptures, or not?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Legatur epistola Palladii, utrum nobis hoc mandaverit: et docebitur quod etiam nunc fallit.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Let the letter of Palladius be read, [to see] whether he sent us this message; and it will be shown that even now he is deceiving.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Sequestrata sit causa Orientalium, sententiam tuam hodie quæro. Arii tibi epistola lecta est. Soles te Arianum negare. Aut damna hodie Arium, aut defende.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Let the case of the Easterners be set aside; today I am asking for your own judgement. The letter of Arius has been read to you. You are accustomed to deny that you are an Arian. Either condemn Arius today, or defend [him].

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dicit : Ut hodie resideremuS, ipse exegisti. Denique etiam hodie tu ipse dixisti, quia Christiani ad Christianos venimus. Christianos nos probasti. Promisisti te conflictaturum, promisisti te allaturum esse rationem. Libenter itaque accepimus præfationem tuam. Optavimus ut quasi Christian is venires. Obtuli tibi epistolam Arii, quam scripsit Arius, de cujns nomine dicitis vos frequenter injuriam sustinerc. Dicitis quod Arium non sequamini. Hodie aperta debet esset sententia. Aut condernna illum, aut astrue quibus vis lectionibus. Et addidit : Ergo, juxta epistolam Arii, Christus Dei Filius non est sempiternus ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose says: You yourself demanded that we sit [in council] today. Indeed, today too you yourself said that we have come as Christians to Christians. You acknowledged us as Christians. You promised that you would engage in debate, you promised that you would give an account. So we gladly accepted your opening statement. We hoped that you would come as to Christians. I put before you the letter of Arius, which Arius wrote, on account of whose name you say that you frequently suffer injury. You say that you do not follow Arius. Today your position ought to be open. Either condemn him, or defend him with whatever readings you wish. And he added: So, according to the letter of Arius, is Christ the Son of God not everlasting?
passages.notes: 'debet esset' read as 'debet esse'.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Omni ore condemnatio facta est in eum qui negaret Dei Filium sempiternum. Ncgavit Arius, hunc sequitur Palladius, qui non vult condemnare Arium. Itaque utrum hujus probanda sententia sit, consideratc : et utrum secundum Scripturas dicat, aut contra Scripturas, intelligere liquet. Lectum est enim : Sempiterna virtus Dei atque divinitas. Dci virtus Christus est. Si igitur sempiterna Dci virtus est, sempiternus utique Christus est, quia Christus est Dei virtus.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: By every mouth condemnation has been pronounced on the one who would deny that the Son of God is everlasting. Arius denied [it]; Palladius follows him, since he does not wish to condemn Arius. So consider whether his position should be approved; and it is clear [enough] to understand whether he speaks according to the Scriptures or against the Scriptures. For it has been read: "The everlasting power of God and [his] divinity." Christ is the power of God. If, therefore, the power of God is everlasting, Christ is certainly everlasting, because Christ is the power of God.

passages.original: Eusebius episcopus dixit: Specialiter dicit solum Patrem sempiternum, et Filium aliquando coepisse?
passages.english: Bishop Eusebius said: Does he explicitly say that the Father alone is everlasting, and that the Son at some point began [to exist]?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Dubitas damnare post divina judicia, cum crepuerit medius? Et addidit: Dicant enim sancti viri legati Gallorum.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Do you hesitate to condemn [him] after the divine judgements, since he burst asunder in the midst? And he added: Let the holy men, the envoys of the Gauls, speak.
passages.notes: 'cum crepuerit medius' alludes to the death of Judas (Acts 1:18) as applied to Arius' death. 'Sancti viri legati Gallorum' are presumably the delegates from Gaul at the Council of Aquileia (381).

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Quid etiam dicit dominus meus Justus ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: What does my lord Justus also say?
passages.notes: Justus is presumably the bishop of Lyon present at the council.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Dicant etiam Afrorum legati, qui omnium civium huc attulere sententias.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Let the envoys of the Africans also speak, who have brought here the opinions of all [their] fellow citizens.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Audite sequentia. Et recitatum est : 'f Solum æternurn, solum sine initio, solum verum, solum immortalitatem habentem. »
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Listen to what follows. And it was read out: "The only eternal, the only one without beginning, the only true, the only one having immortality."
passages.notes: The quotation is from Arius' letter, describing God the Father. The stray marks ''f' and '»' are printed quotation marks and have been left out.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Et in hoc damna eum, qui negat Filium Deum verum. Cum enim ipse sit veritas, quemadmodum non est Deus verus? Et addidit Quid Quid ad hoc?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: On this point too, condemn the one who denies that the Son is true God. For since he is himself the truth, how is he not true God? And he added: What [do you say] to this?
passages.notes: 'Quid Quid' is a duplication in the text and is read as a single 'Quid'.

passages.original: Palladius dixit: Filium verum qui non dicat? Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Arius negavit. Palladius dixit: Cum Apostolus dicat, Christum super omnia Deum, potest aliquis negare verum Filium Dei?
passages.english: Palladius said: Who would not call [him] the true Son? Bishop Ambrose said: Arius denied [it]. Palladius said: Since the Apostle calls Christ God over all, can anyone deny the true Son of God?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Ut scias quam simpli- citer verius a nobi requiratur, ecce dico ego ut dicis, sed semiplenum babeo : cum enim ita dicis, videris negare Deum verum : si autem simpliciter confiteris verum Deum Filium Dei, eo ordine astrue quo ipse propono.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: So that you may know how simply the truer [confession] is required of us: look, I say as you say, but I hold it [to be] half complete. For when you speak in that way, you seem to deny [that he is] true God. But if you simply confess the Son of God [as] true God, affirm [it] in the order in which I myself propose [it].
passages.notes: Several scanning errors have been corrected: 'simpli- citer' to 'simpliciter', 'nobi' to 'nobis', 'babeo' to 'habeo'. 'verius' is odd and may be corrupt; it has been taken as 'the truer [confession]'.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Verum Dominum dicis Filium Dei?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Do you call the Son of God true Lord?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Non quæro tantummodo ut verum Filium dicas, sed ut verum Dominum Dei Filium dicas.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: I am not asking only that you call [him] true Son, but that you call the Son of God true Lord.

passages.original: Cumque Palladius reticeret, Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Solum verum Filium Dei qui dicit, ct non vult dicere Dominum verum, videtur negare. Hoc igitur ordine confiteatur (si tamen confitetur) 491 Palladius, et dicai utrum Dominum Dei Filium dicat?
passages.english: And when Palladius kept silent, Bishop Ambrose said: Whoever calls [him] only the true Son of God, and is unwilling to call [him] true Lord, seems to deny [it]. Let Palladius therefore confess in this order (if indeed he confesses), and let him say whether he calls the Son of God Lord.
passages.notes: Scanning errors have been corrected: 'ct' to 'et', 'dicai' to 'dicat'. The number 491 is a page number from the printed edition and has been omitted.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Joannes dixit in Episto!a sua: Hic eat verus « DeMat (I Joan. v, 20). Nega hoc.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: John said in his Epistle: "This is the true God" (1 John 5:20). Deny this.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "Episto!a" read as "Epistola", "eat" as "est", and "« DeMat" as "Deus". The order "verus Deus" follows the quotation as it appears in p06074.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Et in hoc est fraus. Sic enim soletis dicere unam et veram divinitatem, ut Patris tantummodo, non etiam Filii veram et unamdivinitatem dicatis. Ergo si aperte vis dicere, quia- ad Scripturas me provocas, die quod dixit evangeli- sta Joannes : < Hic est Deus verus, » aut nega dictum.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: In this too there is deceit. For you are accustomed to speak of one and true divinity in such a way that you call it the true and one divinity of the Father only, and not also of the Son. So if you are willing to speak openly, since you challenge me to the Scriptures, say what the evangelist John said, "This is the true God," or deny that it was said.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Non habes libertatem profitendi, ac per hoc, anathema ei qui non confitetur verum Deum Filium Dei.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: You do not have the freedom to profess [it], and for this reason: anathema to him who does not confess that the Son of God is true God.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Filius Dei habet immortalitatem, aut non habet, secundum divinitatem?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Does the Son of God have immortality according to [his] divinity, or does he not?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : De Chri to Filio Dei- quid dicis?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: What do you say about Christ, the Son of God?

passages.original: Eusebius episcopus dixit : Quid superfluis immora- ris? Cum legeretur impietas Arii, qui hoc dicit de Patre, quia solus hahet immortalitatem, attulisti testimonium ad consensum impietatis Arii, ex Apo- stolo, dicens: t Qui solus habet immortalitatem, et lucem habitat inaccessibilem (Ibid.).» Sed si intelligis, totius naturae dignitatem in Dei nomine expr.
passages.english: Bishop Eusebius said: Why do you dwell on superfluous things? When the impiety of Arius was read, who says this of the Father, that he alone has immortality, you brought forward testimony from the Apostle in agreement with the impiety of Arius, saying: "Who alone has immortality, and dwells in unapproachable light" (ibid.). But if you understand, [the Apostle] expressed the dignity of the whole nature in the name of God.
passages.notes: The passage breaks off mid-word ('expr.'); completed from the following context as 'expressit' (expressed).

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Aperte de te sententiam quaero : Filius Dei habet immortalitatem secundum generationem divinam, an non habet?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: I am asking for your opinion openly: does the Son of God have immortality according to [his] divine generation, or does he not?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Non divinitas mortua est, sed caro mortua est.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: It was not the divinity that died, but the flesh that died.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit; Filius Dei secundum di- vinitatem habet immortalitatem, an non habet ? Sed etiam fraudes et insidias tuas non secundum Arii professionem prodidisti. Et addidit: Qui Filium Dei negat habere immortalitatem, quid vobis videtur?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Does the Son of God, according to his divinity, have immortality, or does he not? But you have also betrayed your deceits and snares, not according to the profession of Arius. And he added: What do you think of one who denies that the Son of God has immortality?
passages.notes: The sense of 'non secundum Arii professionem' is unclear; perhaps the text is faulty (one might expect 'secundum', i.e. in line with Arius' profession).

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Astute et hoc, ut de Dei Filio nihil exprimas evidenter. Et ego dico, Immortalitatem habet Dei Filius secundum divinitatem. Aut nega, « qui habet immortalitatem. »
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: This too is cunning, so that you state nothing clearly about the Son of God. And I say: the Son of God has immortality according to [his] divinity. Or else deny [the words] "who has immortality."
passages.notes: "Who has immortality" appears to quote 1 Timothy 6:16.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Secundum carnem. Anima nostra non moritur. Scriptum est enim : < Nolite timere eos qui carnem possunt occideret animam autem non possunt (Matth. X, 28). » Cum igitur anima nostra mori non possit, putas quod Christus secundum divinitatem mortuus sit?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: According to the flesh. Our soul does not die. For it is written: "Do not fear those who can kill the flesh but cannot [kill] the soul" (Matthew 10:28). Since, then, our soul cannot die, do you think that Christ died according to [his] divinity?
passages.notes: "occideret" read as "occidere, et".

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Imo non horreo, sed confiteor, secundum carnem meam. Est enim per quem a mortis vinculis sum revinctus.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: No, I do not shrink [from it], but I confess [it], with respect to my flesh. For he is the one through whom I have been freed from the bonds of death.
passages.notes: "revinctus" (literally "bound back") makes poor sense with "from the bonds of death". The context requires "released", perhaps reading "devinctus" or "resolutus"; the text may be corrupt.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Scriptum est, Christum passum. Secundum carnem igitur passus est, secundum divinitatem habet immortalitatem. Hoc qui negat, diabolus est.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: It is written that Christ suffered. He suffered, therefore, according to the flesh; according to the divinity he has immortality. Whoever denies this is a devil.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Ergo male dixit Arius, cum etiam Filius Dei habeat immortalitatem secundum divinitatem. Et addidit: Bene dixit, an male?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Therefore Arius spoke wrongly, since the Son of God too has immortality according to the divinity. And he added: Did he speak rightly or wrongly?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: 493 Cui non consentis? Anathema illi qui non explicat fidei libertatem.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Whom do you not agree with? Anathema to him who does not set out the freedom of the faith.
passages.notes: "493" is a page or column number from the printed edition and has been omitted. The sense of "explicat fidei libertatem" ("set out the freedom of the faith", perhaps "speak the faith freely") is uncertain without the surrounding exchange.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Cujus ? Patris an et Filii? Et addidit : Multas impietates congessit Arius, ad alias transeamus. Et recitatum est, SOLUM SAPIENTEM.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Whose? The Father's, or the Son's as well? And he added: Arius has heaped up many impieties; let us pass on to others. And there was read out: "ONLY WISE."
passages.notes: "SOLUM SAPIENTEM" ("[the] only wise [one]") is a phrase from Arius' letter being read out at the council.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Ergo Filius non est sapiens, cum sit ipse sapientia? Nam et nos dicimus, quia ex Patre natus est Filius.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Is the Son therefore not wise, when he is himself Wisdom? For we too say that the Son was born of the Father.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Sapiens est, an non?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Is he wise, or not?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Sapiens ergo, cum sit sapientia.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Wise, then, since he is Wisdom.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Etiam sapientem (quan- tum video) Filium Dei Palladius negore conatus est.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Palladius has even tried, as far as I can see, to deny that the Son of God is wise.
passages.notes: Read "quantum" for the split "quan- tum" and "negare" for the scanning error "negore".

passages.original: Cumque Secundianus reticeret, Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Qui tacet, integrum vult habere judicium. Et addidit : Solum Patrem bonum cum dicit, Filium confessus est, an regavit ?
passages.english: And when Secundianus kept silent, Bishop Ambrose said: He who keeps silent wishes to keep his judgement intact. And he added: When he says that the Father alone is good, has he confessed the Son, or denied [him]?
passages.notes: Read "negavit" for the scanning error "regavit".

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Ergo bonus est Christus?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Is Christ, then, good?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Judaei dicebant, bonus est; et Arius negat quia Filius Dei bonus est.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: The Jews used to say, "He is good"; and Arius denies that the Son of God is good.
passages.notes: The sense of "negat quia" is awkward; it is taken as "denies that".

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Et nos bonos genuit, sed non secundum divinitatem. Deum bonum Dei Filium dicis? .
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: He has also begotten us as good, but not according to divinity. Do you call the Son of God the good God?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Vides ergo, quia Chri. stum, bonum Filium, non bonum Deum dicis, quod a te quaeritur. Et addidit : Qui bonum Deum Filium Dei Deum non confitetur, anathema.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: You see, then, that you call Christ a good Son, not a good God, which is what is being asked of you. And he added: Whoever does not confess the Son of God [to be] the good God, God, let him be anathema.
passages.notes: The anathema formula "Qui bonum Deum Filium Dei Deum non confitetur" is awkwardly phrased and is perhaps corrupt; the repeated "Deum" is rendered literally.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Potens est Filius Dei an non ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Is the Son of God powerful or not?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Ergo Arius male dixit. Et addidit: Vel in hoc damnas Arium ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Therefore Arius spoke wrongly. And he added: Do you at least condemn Arius on this point?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Filius Domini Dei polens cst?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Is the Son of the Lord God powerful?
passages.notes: The scanned text reads "polens cst"; it is taken as "potens est".

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Deus bonus est?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Is God good?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Dominum polentem ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: [Do you call him] the powerful Lord?
passages.notes: The scanned text reads "polentem"; it is taken as "potentem". The question is elliptical.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Potentes (t homines sunt. Scriptum cst: i Quid gloriaris in malitia, qui po- tens es in iniquitate (Psal. LI, 3) ? » Et alibi: « Cum infirmor, tunc potetis sum (II Cor. XII, 10). » lllud a te requiro, ut confitearis Dominum potentem esse Dei Filium Christum : aut si negas, astrue. Nam qui unam potentiam dico Patris et Filii, sic Filium Dei dico potentem sicut et Patrem.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Men too are powerful. It is written: "Why do you boast in malice, you who are powerful in iniquity?" (Ps. 51:3). And elsewhere: "When I am weak, then I am powerful" (2 Cor. 12:10). What I require of you is this: that you confess that Christ, the Son of God, is the powerful Lord; or, if you deny it, make your case. For I, who speak of one power of the Father and the Son, call the Son of God powerful just as [I call] the Father.
passages.notes: The scan has several misreadings, each taken in its evident sense: "(t" as "et", "cst" as "est", "i" as an opening quotation mark, "potetis" as "potens", "lllud" as "Illud". "Astrue" is taken as "adstrue" ("make your case"). The psalm reference follows the Vulgate numbering.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Anathema illi qui negat Dominum potentem Christum.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Anathema to him who denies that Christ is the powerful Lord.

passages.original: Ambrosius 495 ep scopus dixit: Per gratiam dedit, an per naturam ? Et hominibus datur judicium.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Did he give [it] by grace, or by nature? Judgement is given to men as well.
passages.notes: "495" is a page or column number from the printed edition and "ep scopus" is a split "episcopus"; both were corrected.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Postea respondebo libi.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: I will answer you afterwards.
passages.notes: Read "libi" as "tibi".

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Filius Dei (sicut lectum est) judex est, aut non?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Is the Son of God a judge (as has been read), or not?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Habes professionem meam, qua respondebo tibi. Interim perlegatur epistola Arii. Et addidit : In epistola Arii invenies et hoc sacrilegium quod tu moliris.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: You have my profession [of faith], by which I will answer you. Meanwhile let the letter of Arius be read through. And he added: In the letter of Arius you will also find this sacrilege which you are attempting.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Scribant tui, qui volunt.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Let those of your people who wish to, write.
passages.notes: This probably refers to recording the proceedings: "let your [scribes] write."

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Et alibi habes : < Qui cum esset in forma Dei, non rapinam arbitratus est esse se æqualem Deo, sed semetipsum exinanivit, formam servi accipiens, in similitudinem hominum factus, obediens usque ad mortem (Philip. i!, 6), » Et addidit : Vides quia in forma Dei æqualis est? i Et formam, inquit, servi accepit. In quo ergo minor est? Secundum formam utiquc servi, non Dci.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: And elsewhere you have: "Who, though he was in the form of God, did not consider it robbery to be equal to God, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men, obedient even to death" (Phil. 2:6). And he added: Do you see that in the form of God he is equal? And he took, it says, the form of a servant. In what respect, then, is he less? Certainly according to the form of a servant, not of God.
passages.notes: The scriptural reference is printed garbled as "Philip. i!, 6" and has been read as Phil. 2:6. A stray "i" in the text was omitted, and "utiquc" and "Dci" were read as "utique" and "Dei".

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Aut die quia secundum divinitatem minor est Filius Dei.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Or else say that the Son of God is less according to his divinity.
passages.notes: Read "die" as "dic".

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Secundum carnem.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: According to the flesh.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Falsari a vobis divinas Scripturas hodie comprobamus. Sic enim scriptum est: « Pacem meam do vobis, pacem meam relinquo vobis. Non turbetur cor vestrum. Non quomodo hic mundus dat, et ego do vobis. Si diligeretis me gauderetis, quia dixi, Vado ad Patrem, quia Pater major me est (Joan. XIV, 27).) Non dixit, Qui me misit, major me est.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Today we prove that the divine Scriptures are being falsified by you. For it is written thus: "My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you. Let your heart not be troubled. Not as this world gives do I also give to you. If you loved me, you would rejoice, because I said, I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I" (John 14:27[–28]). He did not say, "He who sent me is greater than I."
passages.notes: "Et ego do vobis" is rendered literally as "do I also give to you".

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Anathema illi qui ad divinas Scripturas addit aliquid aut minuit.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Anathema to him who adds anything to the divine Scriptures or takes anything away.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus :dixit : Secundum carnem Filius minor est Patre, secundum divinitatem æqualis est Patri. Legi igitur æqualem Dei Filium Patri, sicut jam et prolata exemplaria testantur. Secundum carnem autem quid miraris minorem, cum dixerit se servum, cum dixerit se lapidem, cum dixerit se minorem angelis, quia scriptum est, < Minorasti eum paulo minus ab angelis (Psal. VIII, 6)? »
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: According to the flesh the Son is less than the Father; according to the divinity he is equal to the Father. So I have read that the Son of God is equal to the Father, as the copies already produced also testify. But why are you surprised that [he is] less according to the flesh, since he called himself a servant, since he called himself a stone, since he called himself less than the angels, because it is written, "You made him a little less than the angels" (Ps. 8:6)?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Anathema illi qui ncgat Filium secundum divinitatem æqualem Patri.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Anathema to him who denies that the Son is equal to the Father according to the divinity.
passages.notes: 'ncgat' read as 'negat'.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Subjectus secundum carnis rationem. Cæterum et ipse meministi quia legisti, « Nemo venit ad me, nisi quem Pater attraxerit (Joan. VI, 44). »
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: [He is] subject in respect of the flesh. For the rest, you yourself remember, because you have read, "No one comes to me unless the Father draws him" (John 6:44).

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Et alibi scriptum est: « Fidelia Deus : per quem vocati estis in communionem Filii ejus (I Cor. i, 9).» Ego dico Patrem majorem esse secundum carnis assumptionem, quam suscepit Filius Dei, non secundum divinitatem.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: And elsewhere it is written: "God is faithful, by whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son" (1 Cor. 1:9). I say that the Father is greater according to the assumption of the flesh which the Son of God took up, not according to the divinity.
passages.notes: 'Fidelia' read as 'Fidelis'.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Caro sine anima non loquitur.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Flesh without a soul does not speak.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Deus ergo Filius Dei est secundum divini tatem, et homo est secundum carnem.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: So the Son of God is God according to the divinity, and he is man according to the flesh.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Dicat quia non secundum divinitatem Apostolus dixit subjectum, sed secundum carnem. Scriplum est enim : « Humiliavit semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem (Philip. II, 8). » In quo ergo mortem gustavit?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Let him say that the Apostle called [him] subject not according to the divinity but according to the flesh. For it is written: "He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death" (Phil. 2:8). In what, then, did he taste death?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Non divinilas, sed caro humiliata est atque subjecLa. Et addidit: Creaturam perfectam bene dixit Arius, an male dixit ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Not the divinity, but the flesh was humbled and made subject. And he added: Did Arius speak well or badly in saying "a perfect creature"?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Profitere quod vis.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Declare what you wish.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Cum Arii impietates tegerentur, et impietas tua paritcr condemnata esi, quae consensit Arianæ impietati. Placuit tibi in media epistolæ lectione proponere quod volebas. Responsum tibi est, quemadmodum Patrem majorem dixerit Filius Dei, eo quod secundum carnis susceptionem Filius majorem Patrem dixerit. Proposuisti etiam subjectum esse Filium Dei, et in hoc responsum tibi est, quia subjeclus Filius Dei secundum carnem esi, non secundum divinitatem.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: When the impieties of Arius were being covered over, your impiety too was equally condemned, since it agreed with the Arian impiety. It pleased you, in the middle of the reading of the letter, to put forward what you wanted. You have been answered as to how the Son of God called the Father greater: namely, that the Son called the Father greater according to his taking up of the flesh. You also put forward that the Son of God is subject, and on this too you have been answered, that the Son of God is subject according to the flesh, not according to the divinity.
passages.notes: 'Cum ... tegerentur' is odd ('were being covered'); perhaps a corruption for 'legerentur' ('were being read'), which would suit the context of the reading of the letter.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Omnia vides scribi. Denique quæ scripta sunt, abundant ad tuae impietatis indicium. Et addidit: Creaturam dicis Christum, an negas ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: You see that everything is being written down. In fact, what has been written is more than enough to expose your impiety. And he added: Do you say that Christ is a creature, or do you deny it?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Ante horam citra actam, cum legeretur quia Arius dixit creaturam Christum, negasti. Oblatum est tibi ut damnares perfidiam, noluisti. Vel nunc dic, utrum natus ex Patre Christus sit, an creatus.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Less than an hour ago, when it was read out that Arius said Christ is a creature, you denied [it]. You were offered the chance to condemn the heresy, and you refused. Say now at least whether Christ was born of the Father or created.
passages.notes: 'Ante horam citra actam' is awkward; rendered as 'less than an hour ago'. 'perfidiam' rendered 'heresy' (literally 'faithlessness').

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: AUalus in tractatu Nicæni concilii subscripsit. Neget factum quia venit ad concilium. Dicat hodie utrum subscripserit in tractatu Nicaeni concilii, an non.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Attalus subscribed to the text of the Council of Nicaea. Let him deny the fact, since he has come to the council. Let him say today whether he subscribed to the text of the Council of Nicaea or not.
passages.notes: 'AUalus' is a scanning error for 'Attalus'. 'Neget factum quia venit' is odd; possibly read as 'let him deny [it], since...' or the sense may be ironic or the text corrupt.

passages.original: Cumque Attalus reticeret, Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Attalus presbyter, licet inter Arianos sit, tamen habet auctoritalem loquendi. Libere profiteatur utrum subscripserit in tractatu Nicæni concilii sub episcopo suo Agrippino, an non.
passages.english: And when Attalus kept silent, Bishop Ambrose said: The presbyter Attalus, though he is among the Arians, nevertheless has the right to speak. Let him openly declare whether or not he subscribed to the text of the Council of Nicaea under his bishop Agrippinus.
passages.notes: 'auctoritalem' read as 'auctoritatem'.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Subscripsisti in tractatu concilii Nicæni, aut non?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Did you subscribe to the text of the Council of Nicaea, or not?

passages.original: Cumque Attalus reticeret, Ambrosius episcopus dixit:
passages.english: And when Attalus kept silent, Bishop Ambrose said:
passages.notes: The passage breaks off; Ambrose's words are not given in this unit.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Quia sæpius vult damnari Palladius, qui jam frequenter damnatus est, lego epistolam Arii, quam ille noluit condemnare. Profitemini quod vobis videtur.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Since Palladius, who has already been condemned many times, wants to be condemned yet again, I am reading the letter of Arius, which he refused to condemn. Declare what you think.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Respondi tibi de ma- jore, respondi tibi et de subjecto, nunc et ipse responde.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: I have answered you about the greater, I have answered you also about the subordinate; now you answer too.
passages.notes: 'de majore... de subjecto' refers to the dispute over the Father as 'greater' and the Son as 'subject'; 'ma- jore' is a split word.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Veneras tractaturus, sed posteaqoam objeci tibi, vidisti Arii epistolam, quam damnare noluisti, asserere autem non potes : idcirco nunc refugis et cavillaris. Plenarie ipsam recitato : ad singula die. Utrum Christus creatus videatur, an fuit quando non fuit Christus, an vero semper fuit unigenitus Dei Filius. Cum Arii epistolam audieris, aut damna, aut proba.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: You had come intending to debate, but after I confronted you, you saw the letter of Arius, which you refused to condemn but cannot defend; that is why you now back away and quibble. Read it out in full; speak to each point: whether Christ seems [to you] to be created, or whether there was a time when Christ was not, or whether he was always the only-begotten Son of God. When you have heard the letter of Arius, either condemn it or approve it.
passages.notes: 'posteaqoam' read as 'posteaquam'; 'die' read as 'dic'.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : In consessu fratrum meorum cupio confutari et redargui. Quæ igitur impie dixerim, dicito. Sed impius tibi videor, qui pietatem astruo.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: In the assembly of my brothers I am eager to be refuted and convicted. So say what impious things I have said. But you think me impious, I who am upholding true piety.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Dicis ergo Christum Deum bonum ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: "So do you call Christ the good God?"

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Objecisti me esse im- pium : hoc proba.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: You have charged that I am impious; prove it.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Damna impietatem Arii.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Condemn the impiety of Arius.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Acquiescis ut cætera legantur, Palladi ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Do you agree that the rest be read, Palladius?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Quos quaeritis auditores
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Whom do you want as hearers?
passages.notes: The sentence appears truncated or may be a question; rendered as a question.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Sacerdotes de laicis judicare debent, non laici de sacerdotibus ; sed tamen quos judices petas dicito.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Priests ought to judge laymen, not laymen priests; but nevertheless, say whom you ask for as judges.
passages.notes: 'Sacerdotes' here refers to bishops.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Etsi in multis impietatibus deprehensus sit, erubescimus tamen ut videatur 501 qui sacerdotium sibi vindicat a laicis esse damnatus. Ac per hoc, quoniam et in hoc ipso damnandus est qui laicorum exspectat sententiam, cum magis de laicis sacerdotes debeant judicare, juxta ea quae hodie audivimus Palladium profitentem, et juxta ea quae condemnare noluit, pronuntio illum sacerdotio indignum et curandum ut in loco ejus catholicus ordinetur.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Although he has been caught in many impieties, we are nevertheless ashamed that one who claims the priesthood for himself should appear to have been condemned by laymen. And for this reason, since he deserves condemnation in this very point too, that he awaits the verdict of laymen, when priests ought rather to judge laymen, in accordance with what we have heard Palladius profess today, and in accordance with what he refused to condemn, I pronounce him unworthy of the priesthood, and [declare] that care must be taken that a catholic be ordained in his place.
passages.notes: The number 501 is a page reference from the printed edition and has been omitted.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Imperator clementissi- mus et Christianus sacerdotum judicio causam a, et ut ipsi arbitri essent altercationis in quid constituissemus. Quoniam igitur nobis judicium videtur delatum, interpres est Scriptura : condemnemus Palladium, qui impii Arii noluit damnare sententiam. Et quia ipse Dei Filium sempiternum, et cætera quæ actis hærent, negavit: ergo anathema habeatur.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: The most clement and Christian emperor [has entrusted] the case to the judgement of priests, so that they themselves should be arbiters of the dispute on what we had determined. Since, then, the judgement appears to have been referred to us, Scripture is the interpreter: let us condemn Palladius, who refused to condemn the doctrine of the impious Arius. And since he himself denied that the Son of God is everlasting, and the other things that stand in the record, let him therefore be held anathema.
passages.notes: The text is defective after 'causam a' (a footnote mark follows, and a verb such as 'commisit' appears to be missing); the sense '[has entrusted]' is supplied. 'in quid constituissemus' is also obscure.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Quoniam omnes consistunt viri Christiani, et Deo probati fralres, et consacerdotes nostri, dicat unusquisque quod sibi videtur.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Since all [who are present] stand [here as] Christian men, brothers approved by God, and our fellow priests, let each one say what seems [right] to him.
passages.notes: 'fralres' is a scanning error for 'fratres' (brothers). 'consistunt' may mean simply 'are assembled/present'; rendered 'stand [here as]'.

passages.original: Felix episcopus Jadertinus dixit : Palladium , qui blasphemavit Filium, sicut Arius , cum omnibus nariter condemno.
passages.english: Felix, bishop of Jadera, said: Together with all, I condemn Palladius, who blasphemed the Son, as Arius [did].
passages.notes: 'nariter' read as 'pariter'. Jadera is modern Zadar.

passages.original: 504 Et cum Secundianus subripuisset, Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Audisti, Secundiane, cujusmodi Palladius impius sententiam, sacerdotali concilio damnatus, exceperit. Licet displicuerit nobis, quod ejus, hoc est Palladii non horrueris amentiam, tamen de te aliqua specialiter quaero, utrum Dei Filium Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, vel non verum Deum dicas.
passages.english: And when Secundianus had broken in, Bishop Ambrose said: You have heard, Secundianus, what kind of sentence the impious Palladius has received, condemned by a council of priests. Although it displeased us that you did not shrink from his madness, that is, Palladius', nevertheless I ask certain things of you specifically: whether you call the Son of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, true God or not.
passages.notes: 'subripuisset' is taken as 'interrupted/broke in'; the sense is uncertain. 504 is an edition page number, omitted.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Deum verum Dci Filium confiteris ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Do you confess the Son of God [to be] true God?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Verum Deum dicis?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Do you call [him] true God?

passages.original: Secundianus dixit: Qui fuerit Arius ignoro, quid dixerit nescio : mecum loqueris vivus ad vivum. Illud dico quod Christus dixit: Unigenitum Filium se asserit Patris, Filius unigenitus : Deus est Dei Filius verus.
passages.english: Secundianus said: Who Arius was I do not know; what he said I do not know. You are speaking with me, a living man to a living man. I say what Christ said: he declares himself the only-begotten Son of the Father, the only-begotten Son; he is God, the true Son of God.
passages.notes: The punctuation of the last sentence is uncertain; perhaps 'the only-begotten Son of God is true God'.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Deus vcrus est, verus Deus Filius Deus. Et addidil: In Scripturis divinis scriptum est, « quia qui jurant super terram, jurabunt Deum verum (Isai. LXV, 16). » Quod utique de Christo esse non dubium est. Nos ergo verum Dcum profilemur, et fides nostra hæc est et professio, quia unigenitus Patris Filius, hoc est verus Deus. Die et tu de Deo vero, Dei Filium Deum verum.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: He is true God; the Son, God, is true God. And he added: In the divine Scriptures it is written "that those who swear upon the earth will swear by the true God" (Isaiah 65:16). That this is about Christ there is certainly no doubt. We therefore profess [him] true God, and this is our faith and profession: that the only-begotten Son of the Father is true God. You too say: from true God, the Son of God, true God.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'vcrus' for 'verus', 'addidil' for 'addidit', 'Dcum profilemur' for 'Deum profitemur', 'Die' for 'Dic'. The opening 'Deus verus est, verus Deus Filius Deus' is awkward and may be corrupt.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Filius Dei Deus verus est ?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Is the Son of God true God?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : In hoc fraudem facis, ut non Deum verum dicas, sed Deum unigenitum, ac per hoc die simpliciter : Unigenilus Dei Filius Deus verus.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: In this you are practising deceit, in that you do not say 'true God' but 'only-begotten God'; and therefore say simply: The only-begotten Son of God [is] true God.
passages.notes: 'die' read as 'dic'; 'Unigenilus' as 'Unigenitus'.

passages.original: 505 Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Et qui hoc non confitetur, jure damnatur. Ac per hoc sæpe te convenio, licet cavillando negaveris veritatem. Non quaero ut tantummodo unigenitum Dci, Filium Dei dicas, sed etiam Deum verum.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: And whoever does not confess this is rightly condemned. And for this reason I challenge you repeatedly, although you have denied the truth by quibbling. I do not ask only that you call the only-begotten of God the Son of God, but also true God.
passages.notes: '505' is a page number from the printed edition, omitted. 'Dci' read as 'Dei'.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Qui negat unigenitum Dei Filium, anathema sit.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Whoever denies the only-begotten Son of God, let him be anathema.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Nondum resipuisli. Et adjecit : Ne quid illi videatur esse subreptum , confirmet sententiam suant. Dicat ergo unigenitam Christum, Dei Filium, Deum verum.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: You have not yet come to your senses. And he added: So that nothing may seem to have been slipped past him, let him confirm his statement. Let him therefore say: Christ, the only-begotten, Son of God, [is] true God.
passages.notes: 'resipuisli' read as 'resipuisti', 'suant' as 'suam', 'unigenitam' as 'unigenitum'.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Quid dixisti? Certe si dixisses tanta, quod gloriose dicitur, sæpe repetendum est.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: What did you say? Surely, if you had said so much — what is said to [God's] glory ought to be repeated often.
passages.notes: 'si dixisses tanta' seems corrupt or incomplete (perhaps 'tantum' or 'tanti'); the sentence's construction is uncertain.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Qui dicit ipsum Patrem Filium, sacrilegus est. Hoc a te quaero ut dicas de Deo vero Deum verum Dei Filium natum.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Whoever says that the Father himself is the Son is sacrilegious. What I ask of you is that you say that the Son of God was born true God from true God.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: A Deo vero Deus verus est?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Is he true God from true God?

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Si non dixeris Deum verum de Deo vero natum esse, Christum negisti.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: If you do not say that true God was born of true God, you have denied Christ.
passages.notes: 'negisti' is read as 'negasti' (= negavisti), 'you have denied'.

passages.original: Ambrosius dixit : Hodie afferre debueras : cæterum subterfugere conaris. Professionem a me exige, et professionem a te exigo. Deus verus est Dei Filius?
passages.english: Ambrose said: You ought to have brought [it] today; but you are trying to evade. Demand a profession [of faith] from me, and I demand a profession from you. Is the Son of God true God?
passages.notes: The object of 'afferre' (what Palladius should have brought) is not stated in the passage.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit: Ratione permoveat nos impietas et insipientia tua. Cum dicis Dcum verum unigenitum, non Deum verum dicis, sed verum unigenitum : ac per hoc, ut istam adimas quæstionem , ita responde. Ex Deo vero Deus verus est?
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: Let your impiety and folly move us by reason. When you say 'the true only-begotten God', you are not saying 'true God' but 'true only-begotten'; and therefore, so that you may remove this question, answer thus: Is he true God from true God?
passages.notes: 'Dcum' is read as 'Deum'. The opening sentence is odd in sense ('let your impiety move us by reason'); it may be ironic, or the text may be faulty.

passages.original: Ambrosius dixit: Non confiteris Deum verum, sed vis dicere, verum unigenitum. Et ego unigenitum, sed dico et Deum verum.
passages.english: Ambrose said: You do not confess true God, but you want to say 'true only-begotten'. I too [say] 'only-begotten', but I also say 'true God'.

passages.original: Ambrosius episcopus dixit : Multas quidem et graves haereses novimus a plurimis ebullire, et veneni vice ad intimum pectus canceris sui virus infundere (II Tim. II , 17). Sed vinci illi vel facile possunt, vel facile vitari, quorum prima propositione omne consilium pectoris proditur. At vero hi quibus 507 multa nobiscum paria sunt, facile possunt innoxias mentes et soli Deo deditas , fraudutenta societate percutere, dum malorum suorum virus per bona no- stra defendunt.
passages.english: Bishop Ambrose said: We know indeed that many grave heresies have bubbled up from a great many people, and that like poison they pour the venom of their canker into the inmost heart (2 Tim. 2:17). But those can either be easily overcome or easily avoided whose whole design of heart is betrayed by their first proposition. But those who have many things in common with us can easily strike innocent minds, devoted to God alone, through a deceitful fellowship, while they defend the venom of their evils by means of our good things.
passages.notes: 'canceris' is read as 'cancri' or a variant form, 'canker' (cf. 2 Tim. 2:17). The numeral '507' is a page number from the printed edition and is omitted. 'fraudutenta' is read as 'fraudulenta', and 'no- stra' as 'nostra'.

passages.original: Videtis ergo omnia eos in tractatu ipsorum, non evangelica fide, sed subdola malignitate ad seducendos simplices quosque posuisse. Non jam tam suspectum quam manifestum omnibus esse debet ita eos Deum de Deo posuisse, ut Arius tradere solebat, ut ex Deo factus sit, non ex Deo natus. Qui si natus est, unius substantiae est: si factus est, verus Filius non est, et si verus Filius non est, nec verus Deus est. Aut si verus Deus est et de Patre non est, duo sum habentes singuli et voluntates proprias, et imperia diversa. Vel si concordia tantum et societate unum sunt, non tamen et substantia, verus, ut jam dixi, Deus non est: et sic erit Deus ut Moyses Phanoni (Exod. VII, 1) : potestate, non genere. Filius quoque ita credendus erit, ut per Isaiam populo dictum est: Filios genui et exaltavi (Isai. i, 2), et alihi : Dii estis, et filii Altissimi omnes (Psal. LXXXI, 6). Sed ut primoge litus ita habebitur, quomodo et Israel a Deo primogenitus filius appellatus est (Eud.
passages.english: You see, then, that in their treatise they set down everything not in evangelical faith but with crafty malice, to lead astray all the simple. It ought now to be not so much suspected as plain to all that they set down "God from God" in the way Arius used to teach, namely that he was made from God, not born from God. If he is born, he is of one substance; if he is made, he is not a true Son; and if he is not a true Son, neither is he true God. Or if he is true God and is not from the Father, there are two, each having his own will and separate dominions. Or if they are one only by concord and fellowship, but not also in substance, he is not, as I have already said, true God; and so he will be God as Moses was to Pharaoh (Exod. 7:1): by power, not by kind. He will also have to be believed a Son in the way it was said to the people through Isaiah: "I have begotten sons and exalted [them]" (Isa. 1:2), and elsewhere: "You are gods, and all sons of the Most High" (Ps. 81:6). But he will be held firstborn in the way that Israel too was called by God a firstborn son (Exod.
passages.notes: 'Phanoni' read as 'Pharaoni'; 'primoge litus' as 'primogenitus'; 'Eud.' as 'Exod.'; 'sum' as 'sunt'. The passage ends mid-reference (Exod. 4:22).
